case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Abdul Karim and Others
facts: The State of U.P. has filed this appeal against the judgment passed by a Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court directing acquittal of the three respondents (hereinafter referred to as the 'A-1, A-2 and A-3') respectively.

The accused persons were convicted for the offence punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC') by the IVth Additional and Sessions Judge, Bareilly in Sessions Trial No. 359/78.
Background facts in a nutshell are as follows: ...
The first information report (Ex. Ka. 1) was to the effect that Buddhi was the husband of the complainant (PW-1) whereas A-1, Abdul Karim was his elder brother.
issues: Whether the prosecution has failed to establish its accusations?
Whether the evidence of PWs 1, 2 and 3 leaves no manner of doubt that the respondents were the assailants?
petitioner_arguments: The evidence of PWs 1, 2 and 3 leaves no manner of doubt that the respondents were the assailants and the trial Court had rightly convicted them.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has failed to establish its accusations.
The judgment of acquittal was passed.
court_reasoning: The High Court noted that identification was practically impossible from such a large distance particularly when the field was obstructed by standing crops of sugarcane which were not less than 6-7 ft in height.
The High Court therefore rightly observed that they could not have seen the assaults not only because of the distance but because of the presence of heights of crops of sugarcane.
holding: The appeal fails and is dismissed accordingly.
cases_cited: State of Uttar Pradesh v Abdul Karim
